channel.title: The Honest Software Review
channel.description: Two-minute honest software reviews from hand-researched dossiers: real pricing, the honest knock, and who should skip it. No hype, no fake discounts — and we say skip it when that's the truth.
channel.itunes:author: AIBuilder Marketplace

item.title: Lucrovox: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The meter is AI-handled calls: Starter’s 100 calls a month is roughly three a day, so a genuinely busy shop outgrows it quickly — and the steps are steep ($199 → $499 → $999). Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/lucrovox-review/

item.title: Databox: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The pricing model bites: Pro connects only 3 data sources, so the per-source fees stack up fast — and for agencies juggling many clients with diverse tools it gets expensive. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/databox-review/

item.title: Capsule: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Capsule's simplicity is the product: it deliberately does less than the CRM giants, which is why small teams actually use it. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/capsule-review/

item.title: IDrive: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The first-year price is a teaser and the renewal is the price — IDrive says so itself under the plan table, and on the current numbers the step from discounted to standard is about 43% (Personal 5 TB goes from $6.99 to $9.99 a month). Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/idrive-review/

item.title: Aircall: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Two structural catches: the 3-seat minimum makes the real starting price triple the sticker, and the annual-vs-monthly gap is steep (Professional: $50 vs $70). Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/aircall-review/

item.title: Reclaim.ai: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The magic only works if your team lives in Google Calendar — it's Google-first, so Outlook-heavy shops are out, and the free tier is quite limited. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/reclaim-ai-review/

item.title: Printify: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Printify makes nothing until you sell — the Premium fee only pays off past a break-even order volume, and because it's a middleman marketplace, print quality and shipping vary by the provider you pick. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/printify-review/

item.title: Arbor: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The honest catches: it only exists in deregulated US states, it only touches the supply rate (delivery charges stay with your utility), and the headline savings — Arbor itself reports an average of up to $593/year — depend entirely on how bad your current default rate is. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/arbor-review/

item.title: Velora: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Velora is three acquired products (Keela, Aplos, Raisely) being unified into one platform, and that's the honest watch-out: integration between them is newer than the marketing suggests, so check how deeply the pieces actually connect for your workflow before committing. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/velora-review/

item.title: Hello Bar: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The meter is views, not results: every visitor who sees a popup counts against your quota, so a traffic spike raises the bill regardless of how many emails you actually captured — a busy site outgrows the entry tier fast. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/hello-bar-review/

item.title: VidPal: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Credits don't carry over month to month, and a few users report slow support/account responses — so run the free plan through a full create-and-publish loop before you pay.. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/vidpal-review/

item.title: Shore: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: It's built for local appointment businesses, and that's also the boundary: the integration list is short (calendar, Google, Instagram, Meta), and once you add POS and payments the monthly total climbs well past the entry price. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/shore-review/

item.title: Miro: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Per-member pricing charges for every member added to the workspace, so an org-wide rollout multiplies at full headcount — and the free plan's 3-board cap is workspace-wide, not per person, so real teams outgrow it in days. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/miro-review/

item.title: Descript: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: It's per-editor pricing with two meters running underneath: media hours AND monthly AI credits. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/descript-review/

item.title: ClickUp: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/clickup-review/

item.title: Kit: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Three honest notes. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/kit-review/

item.title: Healthie: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Two honest limits: it's pricier than alternatives with thin mid-tier options, and several users report slow customer service (sometimes a week or more to reply). Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/healthie-review/

item.title: Restream: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The channel caps are the business model — each tier buys a few more destinations, and every extra teammate is a separate $25/mo seat on top of the plan. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/restream-review/

item.title: Survicate: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The plan is metered by response volume, not by surveys — a viral NPS month can push you a tier up, and the free plan's 30-day retention quietly deletes your history. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/survicate-review/

item.title: Feedvisor: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The honest structure: the $100 tier is a limited on-ramp, and most of what Feedvisor is famous for (the algorithmic Buy-Box strategy that holds prices UP, ad management, analysts) lives behind the $1,500+ 360 tier — this is enterprise software for serious catalogs, priced accordingly. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/feedvisor-review/

item.title: Circle: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The sticker is only the entry: Circle keeps a commission on every sale on top of Stripe's processing fees, and email marketing is a separate add-on — so a monetized community's real bill runs meaningfully past the plan price. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/circle-review/

item.title: Auware: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: It's deliberately narrow — Shopify-only and built around segmented paid traffic. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/auware-review/

item.title: AgencyAnalytics: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Two honest snags. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/agencyanalytics-review/

item.title: Heard: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Mind the fine print between tiers: the entry plan does not include your annual tax filing (a ~$750 one-off on Lite), it is annual billing only, and messy back-months cost extra as catch-up fees. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/heard-review/

item.title: Momence: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The 'free' plan is the most expensive one once you have real volume: a 5% commission on every sale overtakes Pro's $60 flat fee around $30k/year in processed revenue. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/momence-review/

item.title: Runpod: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The honest math is utilization. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/runpod-review/

item.title: VEA: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The pitch is unusually bold: an AI that learns your business the way a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/vea-review/

item.title: Wati: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The plan price is the smallest part of the bill. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/wati-review/

item.title: SocialBee: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: You are billed per social profile, not per person, and a profile is one brand account on one network. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/socialbee-review/

item.title: Foxit: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Foxit's whole pitch is being the honest fraction of Acrobat's price, and it largely delivers. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/foxit-review/

item.title: PushOwl: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The bundles are push-first: every paid tier still caps included email at 500 a month, so 'omnichannel' email at any real volume means buying separate credits — and consumption-based pricing gets harder to predict as your sends climb. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/pushowl-review/

item.title: Hostinger: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: The headline price only holds if you prepay years up front — renewals run several times the intro rate, the number-one complaint. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/hostinger-review/

item.title: Aspire: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: It's a fintech account (strongest in Southeast Asia), not a full bank — great for keeping fixed costs near zero on mostly-domestic activity, but confirm it supports your country and currencies before you build your finances around it.. Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/aspire-review/

item.title: Toggl: worth it, or skip it? The honest review
item.description: Toggl's honesty problem is the good kind: the free tier is so capable that many teams never need to pay — the paid line is drawn exactly at 'do you bill clients' (budgets, rates, profitability). Full dossier: https://aibuildermarketplace.com/b2b/toggl-review/
